sentences.zh: 换句话说，他写得太猛了，因为这本书的设计初衷是让它变得越来越恐怖。

sentences.en: And it culminates with horrific murders.
sentences.zh: 它以恐怖的谋杀告终。

sentences.en: I mean, horrible murders.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，可怕的谋杀。

sentences.en: And so as you're reading it, you know that you're kind of getting this sense of crescendo towards absolute violence, darkness, nihilism.
sentences.zh: 所以当你阅读它时，你知道你正在感受到一种向绝对暴力、黑暗和虚无主义的渐强感。

sentences.en: And this is why I think in the aftermath of the Second World
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我认为在第二次世界大战之后，

sentences.en: War, he was so interesting to so many people in France.
sentences.zh: 他在法国引起了那么多人的兴趣。

sentences.en: So many kind of philosophers and thinkers kind of identified the 120 Days of Sodom as a kind of prophecy of the Gestapo, of torture camps and death camps.
sentences.zh: 许多哲学家和思想家将《索多玛120天》视为盖世太保、酷刑营和死亡集中营的预言。

sentences.en: Because it's the story of these four Libertines who basically they're shacked up in this
sentences.zh: 因为这是四个浪荡子的故事，他们基本上躲在

sentences.en: castle and they imprison a vast number of people and subject them to all kinds of horrible kind of tortures.
sentences.zh: 城堡里，囚禁了大量的人，并对他们施加了各种可怕的酷刑。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so the most famous cinematic adaptation of 120 Days of Sodom is by Pasolini, the great Italian director.
sentences.zh: 关于《索多玛120天》最著名的电影改编作品，出自伟大的意大利导演帕索里尼之手。

sentences.en: It's the last film he made called Salo, which was the plot of 120 Days of Sodom set in the kind of the final fascist republic before Mussolini's death.
sentences.zh: 那是他最后一部电影《萨罗》，将《索多玛120天》的情节设定在墨索里尼倒台前夕的最后那个法西斯共和国。

sentences.en: Well, that's a constant obsession, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是一种持续的执念，不是吗？

sentences.en: The idea that fascism and sadism and sexual sadism, sexual deviance are part of the same sort of mixture.
sentences.zh: 那种认为法西斯主义、虐待狂、性虐待以及性变态都属于同一种混合物的观点。

sentences.en: And I think one of the things that kind of justifies this take is the way that I mentioned before, that actually the castle in 120 Days of Sodom is run like a Jesuit school.
sentences.zh: 我认为，这种解读之所以成立，是因为我之前提到的，实际上《索多玛120天》里的城堡运作方式就像一所耶稣会学校。

sentences.en: So it's this attempt to impose order on absolute horror, which of course you get in Auschwitz, you know, the trains, the timetables, the mechanized processes.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一种试图在绝对的恐怖中强加秩序的尝试，当然，你在奥斯威辛集中营也能看到这一点，比如那些火车、时刻表和机械化的流程。

sentences.en: And I think that it's that, that people in the aftermath of the Second World War, when they looked at 120 Days of Sodom, were struck by.
sentences.zh: 我认为正是这一点，让二战后的人们在审视《索多玛120天》时感到震惊。

sentences.en: So the sort of methodically regulated obscenity, basically.
sentences.zh: 基本上就是那种有条不紊、受到严格监管的淫秽行径。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And actually, Saad loses the manuscript of 120 Days of Sodom.
sentences.zh: 事实上，萨德确实弄丢了《索多玛120天》的手稿。

sentences.en: He's written it in secret, very, very small hand, hides it in the brickwork, but loses it because he gets overtaken by the events of the French Revolution.
sentences.zh: 他秘密地用非常非常小的字迹写成，藏在砖墙里，但因为法国大革命的爆发，他被迫转移，结果弄丢了。

sentences.en: So the governor of the Bastille on the 2nd of July, 1789, as the streets of Paris are becoming ever more, you know, starting to seethe, he wrote to a friend and
sentences.zh: 所以，1789年7月2日，当巴黎街头开始变得越来越……你知道，开始沸腾时，巴士底狱的典狱长写信给一位朋友，

sentences.en: reported that the Marquis de Saad had appeared at the window of his cell and shouted with all his
sentences.zh: 报告说萨德侯爵出现在牢房窗前，用尽全身

sentences.en: strength and been heard by the entire neighborhood and by passers-by that they were slaughtering and
sentences.zh: 力气大喊，整个街区和路人都听到了，说他们正在屠杀和

sentences.en: assassinating the prisoners of the Bastille and that people should come to their aid.
sentences.zh: 谋杀巴士底狱的囚犯，人们应该去救他们。

sentences.en: And it's absolutely classic Marquis de Saad that the way he's able to be heard shouting from his window is that he takes what was called a pissing tube.
sentences.zh: 这非常符合萨德侯爵的典型作风，他之所以能从窗户大喊并被人听到，是因为他用了一个所谓的“排尿管”。

sentences.en: So it was a kind of piece of metal that the prisoner would have to piss through out into the kind of the sewer down below.
sentences.zh: 那是一种金属管，囚犯必须通过它向外排尿，通往下面的下水道。

sentences.en: So he's shouting through that.
sentences.zh: 所以他是对着那个管子大喊。

sentences.en: And this does play a part in inciting the mob that two days later will ransack the Bastille and end up chopping the head of the governor off and parading around on a spike.
sentences.zh: 这确实在煽动暴民方面起到了作用，两天后，暴民洗劫了巴士底狱，最终砍下了典狱长的头，并挑在长矛上游行示众。

sentences.en: But by that point, the Marquis de Saad himself is not there because he's been transferred.
sentences.zh: 但到那时，萨德侯爵本人已经不在那里了，因为他被转移了。

sentences.en: He gets taken to an asylum for the insane, a place called Charenton, again, on the outskirts of Paris.
sentences.zh: 他被带到了一个精神病院，一个叫沙朗通的地方，同样是在巴黎郊区。

sentences.en: And he loses the manuscript of 120 days.
sentences.zh: 他弄丢了《120天》的手稿。

sentences.en: While he's being transferred.
sentences.zh: 就在他被转移的时候。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Just a quick question there, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，有个小问题。

sentences.en: So he's transferred to a lunatic asylum.
sentences.zh: 所以他被转移到了精神病院。

sentences.en: You wouldn't say he was a lunatic, would you?
sentences.zh: 你不会说他是疯子，对吧？

sentences.en: You'd say he was completely irrational.
sentences.zh: 你会说他完全是不理智的。

sentences.en: Yes, I think so.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想是这样。

sentences.en: I mean, I wouldn't say that he was normal, but I think that saying he's mad is a kind of cop out.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我不会说他正常，但我认为说他疯了是一种逃避。

sentences.en: But I think the fact that he keeps being transferred to, well, he's either being
sentences.zh: 但我认为，他不断被转移到……嗯，他要么被

sentences.en: imprisoned or transferred to asylums does suggest that it doesn't matter whether it's the monarchical
sentences.zh: 监禁，要么被转移到精神病院，这确实表明，无论是君主制

sentences.en: regime or the revolution regime, people find him very, very difficult to cope with.
sentences.zh: 政权还是革命政权，人们都觉得他非常非常难以应付。

sentences.en: But with the revolution, he can play the part of someone who'd suffered from despotic tyranny.
sentences.zh: 但在革命时期，他可以扮演一个遭受专制暴政迫害的人的角色。

sentences.en: And so in spring 1790, he's freed.
sentences.zh: 所以1790年春天，他被释放了。

sentences.en: He doesn't go back to René because by this point, René has become deeply religious and deeply upset by his arguments.
sentences.zh: 他没有回到蕾妮身边，因为此时的蕾妮已经变得非常虔诚，对他那些论点感到非常不安。

sentences.en: And so refuses to see him and in fact, divorces him two months after his release.
sentences.zh: 所以她拒绝见他，事实上，在他获释两个月后就和他离婚了。

sentences.en: And on top of that, he has money problems because of course, he's an aristocrat in a revolutionary world.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，他还有经济问题，因为在革命世界里，他毕竟是个贵族。

sentences.en: And so he tries to make money by his pen.
sentences.zh: 所以他试图靠笔杆子赚钱。

sentences.en: So he writes a play, it gets staged for one night.
sentences.zh: 他写了一部剧本，上演了一晚。

sentences.en: Predictably, there's a massive riot to get smashed up.
sentences.zh: 不出所料，引发了大规模骚乱，被砸了个稀巴烂。

sentences.en: And he's writing various novels, most famously, Justine, The Sufferings of Virtue, which we'll come to a bit later.
sentences.zh: 他还写了各种小说，最著名的是《瑞斯丁：美德的不幸》，我们稍后会谈到。

sentences.en: But again, he hasn't lost his charm, despite the fact that while he was in the Bastille, he'd actually become quite obese.
sentences.zh: 但话说回来，尽管他在巴士底狱期间变得相当肥胖，但他并没有失去魅力。

sentences.en: He hitches up with a former actress called Marie Constance Quinet.
sentences.zh: 他与一位名叫玛丽·康斯坦斯·基内的前女演员好上了。

sentences.en: But what he really does is throw himself into revolutionary politics because he has this certain degree of prestige from having been a prisoner in the Bastille.
sentences.zh: 但他真正做的是投身于革命政治，因为他曾是巴士底狱的囚犯，这让他拥有了一定的声望。

sentences.en: So he casts himself as Citoyen Sade, Citizen Sade, and he registers himself in the most radical quarter of Paris.
sentences.zh: 于是他自称为“萨德公民”，并在巴黎最激进的区登记注册。

sentences.en: So the Place de Vendôme, which later comes to be called the Section des Piques.
sentences.zh: 也就是旺多姆广场，后来被称为“长矛区”。

sentences.en: And this is the stamping ground of Rose Pierre himself.
sentences.zh: 那是罗伯斯庇尔本人的大本营。

sentences.en: And Sade seems to actually have done this with some commitment and some sense of duty.
sentences.zh: 萨德似乎确实对此投入了一些承诺和责任感。

sentences.en: I mean, he gets voted onto a three-man committee that is charged with inspecting girls' orphanages.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他被选入了一个三人委员会，负责视察女子孤儿院。

sentences.en: That's a terrible, terrible mistake, surely.
sentences.zh: 这肯定是个非常非常糟糕的错误。

sentences.en: Me, the Marquis de Sade, the girls' orphanage.
sentences.zh: 我，萨德侯爵，去女子孤儿院？

sentences.en: What were they thinking?
sentences.zh: 他们到底在想什么？

sentences.en: Oh, no.
sentences.zh: 哦，不。

sentences.en: But he actually, I mean, he seems to have executed his duties responsibly.
sentences.zh: 但他实际上……我的意思是，他似乎负责任地履行了他的职责。

sentences.en: He leads an inquiry into hospital conditions, again, with great responsibility.
sentences.zh: 他领导了一项关于医院状况的调查，同样表现得非常有责任感。

sentences.en: And the really fascinating example of the way that he seems not to have allowed his violent fantasies to influence his
sentences.zh: 一个非常迷人的例子是，他似乎没有让自己的暴力幻想影响到他

sentences.en: behavior as a kind of revolutionary official is that he ends up being elected president of the
sentences.zh: 作为革命官员的行为，他最终被选为

sentences.en: Section des Piques.
sentences.zh: 长矛区的主席。

sentences.en: And in that role, he has to work out who should be sent for trial as enemies of the revolution, who shouldn't.
sentences.zh: 在这个职位上，他必须决定谁应该作为革命的敌人被送上审判，谁不应该。

sentences.en: And on the list of people who could conceivably be sent to trial are his in-laws.
sentences.zh: 而在可能被送上审判的名单中，有他的姻亲。

sentences.en: And he doesn't send them to trial.
sentences.zh: 但他没有把他们送去审判。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So he doesn't seek revenge on his mother-in-law who had him in prison for 13 years.
sentences.zh: 所以他没有向那位让他坐了13年牢的岳母寻求报复。

sentences.en: No, he doesn't.
sentences.zh: 没有，他没有。

sentences.en: To his credit, I think.
sentences.zh: 我认为这值得称赞。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He doesn't behave at all as a monster during the revolutionary period.
sentences.zh: 在革命期间，他的表现一点也不像个怪物。

sentences.en: Quite the opposite, in fact.
sentences.zh: 事实上，恰恰相反。

sentences.en: And it may be that that is actually the sense that perhaps he's too soft, ironically, is what leads to his downfall.
sentences.zh: 也许正是因为他太心软了，讽刺的是，这反而导致了他的垮台。

sentences.en: Because it seems that Rose Pierre decides that he is a counter-revolutionary.
sentences.zh: 因为罗伯斯庇尔似乎认定他是一个反革命分子。

sentences.en: And so December 1794, he's jailed in the horrible conditions that suspects are put into during the height of the terror.
sentences.zh: 所以1794年12月，他被关进了恐怖统治时期嫌疑人所处的恶劣环境中。

sentences.en: For six weeks, he said, I slept in the toilet with seven other people.
sentences.zh: 他说，有六周时间，我和另外七个人睡在厕所里。

sentences.en: And he's imprisoned.
sentences.zh: 他被监禁了。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Because he was a former aristocrat or because he has been behaving badly again with servants and so on?
sentences.zh: 是因为他曾是贵族，还是因为他又在仆人身上表现恶劣等等？

sentences.en: No, it's not behaving badly.
sentences.zh: 不，不是因为表现恶劣。

sentences.en: He is accused of being a very immoral suspect man, unfit for society.
sentences.zh: 他被指控为一个非常不道德的嫌疑人，不适合社会。

sentences.en: But that's based on records from decades previously.
sentences.zh: 但这基于几十年前的记录。

sentences.en: All the various escapades he'd been going through before his imprisonment.
sentences.zh: 他入狱前经历过的各种冒险。

sentences.en: He is an aristocrat.
sentences.zh: 他是个贵族。

sentences.en: So that counts against him.
sentences.zh: 所以这对他不利。

sentences.en: And also he has had sons.
sentences.zh: 而且他还有儿子。

sentences.en: And some of these sons have gone abroad to serve with the counter-revolutionary forces.
sentences.zh: 其中一些儿子出国加入了反革命军队。

sentences.en: So again, that isn't a good look for him.
sentences.zh: 所以这对他的形象也不好。

sentences.en: So with that against his name at the height of the terror, I mean, it looks really terrible.
sentences.zh: 因此，在恐怖统治的高峰期，他的名字背负着这些罪名，看起来真的很糟糕。

sentences.en: So Marie Constance, his partner, is able to dole out bribes and get him moved to a better prison, a former convent in Picpus.
sentences.zh: 所以他的伴侣玛丽·康斯坦斯能够通过行贿，让他被转移到条件更好的监狱，即皮克普斯的一座前修道院。

sentences.en: And that is where, almost directly under his window, the guillotine gets set up.
sentences.zh: 就在那里，几乎就在他的窗下，断头台被架设起来了。

sentences.en: It gets removed from the Place de la Concorde and set up underneath his window.
sentences.zh: 它从协和广场被移走，架设在他的窗下。

sentences.en: And so he's smelling the blood that's spilling out from the guillotine.
sentences.zh: 所以他闻到了从断头台溅出的血腥味。

sentences.en: Yeah, because this is the height of the terror.
sentences.zh: 是的，因为这是恐怖统治的高峰期。

sentences.en: I think you said it was December 1794, but it's 1793, isn't it, when he's jailed?
sentences.zh: 我想你刚才说是1794年12月，但应该是1793年，他入狱的时候，对吧？

sentences.en: Sorry, yes.
sentences.zh: 抱歉，是的。

sentences.en: So, I mean, this is the point at which the revolution is beleaguered within and without.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，这是革命在内外受困的时刻。

sentences.en: They're searching for enemies.
sentences.zh: 他们正在搜寻敌人。

sentences.en: So you can completely see why they would identify somebody like him, an aberrant figure, an aristocratic figure, as an enemy within, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以完全理解为什么他们会把像他这样的人，一个反常的人物，一个贵族人物，视为内部的敌人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And amazingly, he is sentenced for execution on the 27th of July, 1794.
sentences.zh: 令人惊讶的是，他在1794年7月27日被判处死刑。

sentences.en: He avoids being taken away.
sentences.zh: 他避免了被带走。

sentences.en: And it may be that that, again, is because Marie Constance has a judicious bribe, but it's
sentences.zh: 这可能再次归功于玛丽·康斯坦斯的一次明智的贿赂，但这也是

sentences.en: also luck because the 27th of July, 1794 is the day that Rosepierre is overthrown and executed the following day.
sentences.zh: 运气，因为1794年7月27日正是罗伯斯庇尔被推翻并于次日被处决的日子。

sentences.en: And so effectively, it's the end of the terror.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，恐怖统治结束了。

sentences.en: Crikey, it is, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 天哪，确实是这样，不是吗？

sentences.en: It's Termidor.
sentences.zh: 那是热月政变。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's the climax of the French Revolution in some ways.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，这是法国大革命的高潮。

sentences.en: So he's that close to execution.
sentences.zh: 所以他离死刑只有一步之遥。

sentences.en: But again, he's able to, having been in the Bastille just before it stormed, he's at the heart of the terror when Rosepierre is executed.
sentences.zh: 但话说回来，他能在巴士底狱被攻占前夕身处其中，又在罗伯斯庇尔被处决时身处恐怖统治的核心。

sentences.en: He's set free October 1794.
sentences.zh: 他在1794年10月获释。

sentences.en: You know, and this is when the terror is kind of subsiding.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那时恐怖统治正在消退。

sentences.en: So he can lead a moderately normal life from this point on, but he's, he's absolutely kind of skint.
sentences.zh: 所以从那时起，他可以过上相对正常的生活，但他绝对是身无分文。

sentences.en: He hasn't really got any money at all.
sentences.zh: 他几乎没有任何钱。

sentences.en: He gets a job as a prompter at the theater in Versailles.
sentences.zh: 他在凡尔赛的剧院找了一份提词员的工作。

sentences.en: He sells Lacoste in 1796, his ancestral home.
sentences.zh: 他在1796年卖掉了他的祖宅拉科斯特。

sentences.en: He's endlessly kind of trying to catch money off people.
sentences.zh: 他不断地试图从别人那里弄钱。

sentences.en: And he starts writing novels again.
sentences.zh: 他又开始写小说了。

sentences.en: And the most notorious novel, as I mentioned before, is this novel, Justine.
sentences.zh: 正如我之前提到的，最臭名昭著的小说是《瑞斯丁》。

sentences.en: There are various iterations of it.
sentences.zh: 它有各种版本。

sentences.en: He just kind of keeps writing and writing and writing it.
sentences.zh: 他只是不停地写啊写啊写。

sentences.en: And basically it's a parody.
sentences.zh: 基本上这是一部戏仿作品。

sentences.en: It's a parody of a novel by the English writer, Samuel Richardson, Pamela.
sentences.zh: 它是对英国作家塞缪尔·理查森的小说《帕梅拉》的戏仿。

sentences.en: Oh, Pamela.
sentences.zh: 哦，《帕梅拉》。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And this is a story of a virtuous girl whose virtue ends up being rewarded.
sentences.zh: 这是一个关于一个美德少女的故事，她的美德最终得到了回报。

sentences.en: The twist in Justine is that she's incredibly virtuous.
sentences.zh: 《瑞斯丁》的转折在于她极其美德。

sentences.en: And every time she does something good, awful things happen to her.
sentences.zh: 每当她做一件好事，可怕的事情就会发生在她身上。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, she has a sister, Juliet, who is the embodiment of vice.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，她有一个妹妹朱丽叶，是邪恶的化身。

sentences.en: And every time she does something awful, you know, she reaps enormous fortunes.

sentences.en: And in it, he writes this little essay called Yet Another Effort, Frenchman, If You Would Become Republicans.
sentences.zh: 在书中，他写了一篇名为《法国人，再加把劲，如果你想成为共和主义者》的小短文。

sentences.en: So he's writing this in the kind of the revolutionary period.

sentences.en: And basically, he is trying to construct a framework of morals that can be rooted in nature rather than in the inheritance of Christianity,
sentences.zh: 基本上，他试图构建一个植根于自然而非基督教遗产的道德框架，

sentences.en: which is being thrown aside as a legacy of despotism.
sentences.zh: 基督教正作为专制主义的遗产被抛弃。

sentences.zh: 他主张一种绝对无可挑剔的进步原则。

sentences.zh: 他绝对支持女性解放，认为女性应该拥有绝对的平等，女性应该有堕胎权，

sentences.zh: 还有我们所说的同性恋权利，即同性恋者在法律面前应享有绝对平等，所有这些都让他听起来像是一个21世纪的进步人士。

sentences.en: But what makes him unsettling for the 21st century as for the 18th and 19th century is that he then starts to push these principles to incredibly unsettling ends.
sentences.zh: 但让他像在18、19世纪一样在21世纪也令人不安的是，他随后开始将这些原则推向极其令人不安的极端。

sentences.en: I mean, in a way, when he talks about the fact that there should be absolute tolerance, he goes further.
sentences.zh: 我是说，在某种程度上，当他谈到应该有绝对的宽容时，他走得更远了。

sentences.en: And rather like trans campaigners now, there's the assumption that a properly revolutionary and progressive state should
sentences.zh: 就像现在的跨性别活动家一样，有一种假设认为，一个真正革命和进步的国家应该

sentences.en: constantly be looking for frontiers to push back, that there will always be people who are suffering because of their sexuality or their gender identity or whatever.
sentences.zh: 不断寻找边界去突破，总会有因为性取向或性别认同等原因而受苦的人。

sentences.en: And that it's the responsibility of a progressive state to push and push and push this forward to undermine what convention calls virtuous and normal.
sentences.zh: 而进步国家的责任就是不断推动、推动、再推动，去破坏那些传统所谓的“美德”和“正常”。

sentences.en: And inevitably, being the Marquis de Sade, he starts to argue that there should be no limit to tolerance for sexual desire at all.
sentences.zh: 不可避免地，作为萨德侯爵，他开始主张对性欲望的宽容应该毫无限制。

sentences.en: So therefore, rape should be legitimate, that incest should be legitimate.
sentences.zh: 因此，强奸应该是合法的，乱伦也应该是合法的。

sentences.en: You know, this is particularly the case for a society like revolutionary France, which is founded on the ideal of fraternity.
sentences.zh: 你知道，对于像革命时期的法国这样建立在博爱理想之上的社会来说，情况尤其如此。

sentences.en: So he's kind of turning the political ideals, you know, turning on his head.
sentences.zh: 所以他是在颠覆政治理想，你知道，将其彻底颠倒过来。

sentences.en: He then starts arguing that murder sustains
sentences.zh: 他随后开始主张谋杀维持着

sentences.en: So he praises the spectacle in China of children's corpses clogging rivers and declares that it is both necessary and politic to erect barriers to population growth in a Republican
sentences.zh: 所以他赞美中国儿童尸体堵塞河流的景象，并宣称在共和政府中建立人口增长障碍既必要又符合政治利益。

sentences.en: government.

sentences.zh: 所以很有趣的是，汤姆，他是在1790年代写下这些的，当时，

sentences.en: you know, your Saint-Just or your Robespierre, they and their rhetoric are sometimes not far short of that.

sentences.en: Their calls for constant terror, their insistence that blood must be spilled to maintain the purity of the revolution.
sentences.zh: 他们呼吁不断的恐怖，坚持必须流血来维持革命的纯洁性。

sentences.en: De Sade is pushing that to its ultimate extreme, but it's not unrooted in the circumstances of the day.
sentences.zh: 萨德将这一点推向了极致，但这并非没有植根于当时的现实环境。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, it's basically implied, hadn't it, that it was one of the causes of the sort of decline of Rome from the glories of the Antonine Age.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这基本上是言下之意，不是吗？认为这是导致罗马从安敦尼王朝的辉煌中衰落的原因之一。

sentences.en: And this is only a few decades after Gibbon was writing, right?
sentences.zh: 而这距离吉本写作的年代才过了几十年，对吧？

sentences.zh: 是的，但这是一种更尖锐的版本。

sentences.en: And he further extrapolates that because they went soft, therefore they were no longer willing to tolerate that
sentences.zh: 他进一步推论，因为他们变得软弱，所以他们不再愿意容忍

sentences.zh: 而且是以绝对萨德式的措辞。当萨德在他的小说中引用古代文献作为

sentences.zh: 冷酷且毫无意义的，弱者就该任其死亡时，他基本上就是在做纳粹所做的事。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.zh: 正如他为所谓的进步国家为何能许可

sentences.zh: 所以我认为他是一个非常令人不安的人物，而且至今仍是如此。

sentences.en: It's interesting how he contains so much.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，他竟然包含了如此多的内容。

sentences.en: So as you say, prefiguring the ethos of fascism, the moral ethos of fascism or something, but also in his emphasis on nature dictates your desires
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，预示了法西斯的精神气质，法西斯的道德风气之类的，但同时他强调自然决定了你的欲望，

sentences.en: to lead an authentic, properly virtuous life, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 我想，为了过上一种真实、真正有德行的生活。

sentences.en: You should act on those desires and for society to try to contain them is wrong and all that sort of stuff.
sentences.zh: 你应该顺应这些欲望，而社会试图压制它们是错误的，诸如此类。

sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这感觉非常、非常现代。

sentences.zh: 确实如此，这就是为什么萨德利用所有这些论点，将它们推向了可怕的极端。

sentences.en: It retains its power to shock and unsettle in the 21st century.
sentences.zh: 它在21世纪依然保留着震撼和不安的力量。
